accepted_step.derivation: From accepted step 1, the state space is Z4 x Z3, with 12 states, and both input symbols give deterministic transitions F0(s,t)=((s+t) mod 4,(t+1) mod 3) and F1(s,t)=((2s+t+1) mod 4,(s+t) mod 3). Define N_{k,j}(s,t) as the number of length-k input prefixes that contain exactly j ones and drive the initial state (1,0) to state (s,t). The empty prefix is length 0, has zero ones, and leaves the machine at (1,0), so N_{0,0}(1,0)=1, and all other N_{0,j}(s,t)=0. For the recurrence, take a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones ending at (s,t). Its last bit is either 0 or 1, a disjoint partition. If the last bit is 0, deleting it gives a length-k prefix with j ones ending at some (u,v) such that F0(u,v)=(s,t). Conversely, each such length-k prefix appends 0 to give a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones ending at (s,t), and distinct prefixes give distinct extensions. Thus the last-bit-0 contribution is the sum of N_{k,j}(u,v) over all (u,v) with F0(u,v)=(s,t). If the last bit is 1, deleting it gives a length-k prefix with j-1 ones ending at some (u,v) such that F1(u,v)=(s,t), and conversely appending 1 gives the required prefix. Thus the last-bit-1 contribution is the sum of N_{k,j-1}(u,v) over all (u,v) with F1(u,v)=(s,t). Adding the disjoint cases gives the recurrence, with out-of-range terms such as j-1<0 or j>k treated as zero. No probabilities are needed for this counting step.
accepted_step.goal: Define count table N_{k,j}(s,t) as the number of length-k prefixes with j ones ending at state (s,t); initialize N_{0,0}(1,0)=1 and update by summing F_0 and F_1 transitions.
accepted_step.result: N_{0,0}(1,0)=1 and all other N_{0,j}(s,t)=0. For k+1>=1, N_{k+1,j}(s,t)=sum over (u,v) with F0(u,v)=(s,t) of N_{k,j}(u,v) + sum over (u,v) with F1(u,v)=(s,t) of N_{k,j-1}(u,v), over Z4 x Z3, with j ranging 0..k+1 and out-of-range terms zero.

use.method: Check the recurrence publicly by tracking one length-1 prefix in each branch and comparing to enumeration. Start from N_{0,0}(1,0)=1. For k=0, j=0: appending 0 gives F0(1,0)=((1+0) mod4,(0+1) mod3)=(1,1), so N_{1,0}(1,1) gets 1. Appending 1 gives F1(1,0)=((2*1+0+1) mod4,(1+0) mod3)=(3,1), so N_{1,1}(3,1) gets 1. The returned formula gives exactly these two nonzero contributions, with j-1<0 handled as zero. For k=1, check j=1 into F1 from (1,1): F1(1,1)=((2*1+1+1) mod4,(1+1) mod3)=(0,2), so a 01 prefix of length 2 with one 1 ends at (0,2); the formula adds N_{1,0}(1,1) to N_{2,1}(0,2). This matches direct composition of the two deterministic transitions. Thus the disjoint last-bit partition, inverse-preimage sums, initial condition, and j-range convention reproduce the returned recurrence.
use.result: The returned step 3 recurrence reproduces the counting table update from F0 and F1 and initializes N_{0,0}(1,0)=1 with all other N_{0,j}=0; the checked samples agree.
